Asha — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a short appendix (redwood-pricing-appendix.xlsx) and a one-page playbook below. High level first: we can offer both a marginal "staircase" per-token ladder and an optional blended committed rate. The tradeoffs are predictable: marginal rewards over time as you pass breakpoints; blended simplifies budgeting but requires a larger commit.

Proposed marginal ladder (example, per token):
- 0–50M tokens / month: $0.00060 per token
- 50M–200M tokens / month: $0.00040 per token (marginal for tokens in this band)
- >200M tokens / month: $0.00025 per token

Blended alternative (example):
- 12-month commit, 3B tokens/year -> blended $0.00038 per token (flat across usage)

Key commercial mechanics we recommend:
- Quarterly true-up: usage is measured monthly, invoiced monthly, with quarterly true-up to settle differences against committed minimums.
- Overage protection: 10% burst credit buffer for each month; sustained overages billed at next-tier marginal rates or converted into a temporary blended uplift if usage stabilizes above commit.
- Step-down glidepath: tiers only move forward (no retroactive discounts), true-up only applies forward-looking adjustments.

I'll follow with a worked example comparing costs and effective per-token under both approaches. Attaching appendix with a calculator.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni

Tom — good questions. Below are straightforward, reproducible examples and our recommended contractual language for handling variability.

Scenario A — marginal (staircase) pricing math (monthly usage = 300M tokens):
- 0–50M @ $0.00060 = 50,000,000 * 0.00060 = $30,000
- 50–200M (150M) @ $0.00040 = 150,000,000 * 0.00040 = $60,000
- 200–300M (100M) @ $0.00025 = 100,000,000 * 0.00025 = $25,000
Total monthly cost (marginal): $115,000
Effective per-token (marginal) = $115,000 / 300,000,000 = $0.0003833... (~$0.00038)

Scenario B — blended commit: 12-month, 3B token commit -> blended $0.00038 per token
Total monthly cost (blended) = 300,000,000 * 0.00038 = $114,000
Effective per-token (blended) = $0.00038

Observation: for this ramp point (300M), blended is marginally cheaper by ~$1k/month. The marginal model gives better upside if you spike beyond the highest tier or if growth is uneven because you only pay lower rates for tokens in higher bands. Blended gives budget certainty and is slightly advantageous when usage is close to the commit run-rate.

Recommended contract language (short):
- Quarterly true-up with monthly metering; committed minimum = X tokens per quarter (to be defined).
- 10% monthly burst buffer at no additional charge; sustained overages beyond buffer billed at marginal band and counted toward the next quarter's true-up.
- Option to convert to a blended pricing for the contract year if the customer signs an annual commitment > 2.5B tokens; conversion requires 30 days' notice.

Operational note: we can model both sides in the attached spreadsheet; I put a "sensitivity" tab that shows effective per-token vs. usage for both approaches so AlphaTech finance can test scenarios.

Links: HubSpot deal RDW-2026-AT-1742 (see notes and current consumption assumptions).

If this direction looks good, we can draft a short SOW + DocuSign to lock the first-year commit and add a one-time onboarding credit (suggested concession discussed below).

—Vivek
